scope: Verified the byte-oriented MD5 implementation against local RFC 1321 (April 1992), SHA-256/384/512 against local FIPS 180-4 (August 2015), and AES-128/256 against local FIPS 197-upd1 (May 2023), including constants, padding, schedules, round order and the printed numeric examples. This extends the ISO 32000-2:2020 sponsored EC3 audit of clauses 7.6, 7.3, 7.5.5 and Table D.3, including Algorithm 2.B digest selection and truncation. SP 800-38A CBC and RFC 6229 vector attribution remain pending because their texts are unavailable; RC4 has corroborating implementation/vector evidence, not a normative-standard verification. Separately linked NIST worked examples are not supplied locally. SASLprep, host-codepage conversion, R5 extension provenance, crypt-filter text conflicts and document integration retain the qualifications below; this is not a complete PDF conformance or side-channel certification.

requirements.gaps: The public APIs accept byte-aligned messages only. SHA-256 and SHA-384/512 are verified within the standard message-length ranges (less than 2^64 and 2^128 bits respectively); counter overflow wraps and is outside that claim. FIPS 180-4 Appendix A.2 points to separate worked digest examples, which are not available locally; existing digest values are independently corroborated with Python hashlib, not claimed as printed FIPS examples.
requirements.known_answer_coverage: All seven RFC 1321 Appendix A.5 messages rechecked; all 64 MD5 constants and shifts; all 144 SHA-2 constants and 24 initial words; the printed FIPS 180-4 abc padding examples; SHA-256/384/512 empty, abc, multi-block and million-a fixed digests, streaming splits, and independent Python hashlib boundary comparisons for byte lengths 0 through 261. Algorithm 2.B final SHA-256/384/512 branch vectors preserve full intermediate digests and select the leftmost 32 bytes only at the end.

clauses: FIPS 197-upd1 sections 3.4-3.5, 4.1-4.4, 5.1-5.3.4; Tables 3-6; Appendices A.1, A.3, B and C
requirements.gaps: AES-128/256 algorithm and the examples printed in FIPS 197-upd1 are verified. Its Appendix C links to a separate examples document; the older Appendix-C-attributed block values remain corroborating tests rather than values rechecked in the 2023 text. SP 800-38A and RFC 6229 are still unavailable locally: CBC mode and RC4 vector locators/attribution remain pending. AES-192 and a constant-time implementation are outside the supported scope.
requirements.known_answer_coverage: All 256 forward and 256 inverse AES substitution entries; all 44 AES-128 and 60 AES-256 expansion words from Appendices A.1/A.3; Appendix B cipher output and all 39 intermediate states, inverse transformations, and fixed-ciphertext decryption. Existing older Appendix-C-attributed AES-128/256 block tests, four-block SP-800-38A-attributed CBC-128/256 tests, and RFC-6229-attributed RC4 tests for seven key sizes and offsets 0,16,256 are retained. Python AES/RC4 self-checks independently corroborate the fixed attributed values; they do not establish primary-source provenance.

requirements.gaps: Document-layer dictionary and crypt-filter discrepancies are listed under integration_findings; Table 25 Length wording is internally inconsistent.

clauses: Adobe Supplement to ISO 32000-1, extension level 3
requirements.gaps: Table 21 prohibits R=5 in conforming PDF 2.0. Compatibility support remains separate; the Adobe extension text is unavailable locally.
requirements.permissions_policy: Password-authenticated keys report Validated or Inconsistent(PermissionsCheck); the document caller owns strict/reported-repair policy. Structural errors remain Syntax.

requirements.gaps: Only printable ASCII preprocessing is supported; other input returns security.saslprep before truncation. RFC 4013/3454 are not locally verified. Document-layer findings remain open.
requirements.permissions_policy: Password-authenticated keys report Validated or Inconsistent(PermissionsCheck); the document caller owns strict/reported-repair policy. Structural errors remain Syntax.

tests: crypto/dictionary-* vector inputs and explicit API expectations
requirements.gaps: Integration findings below are not fixes to the document crate and are not counted as conformance successes.

Report a Perms disagreement through Inconsistent rather than choosing recovery in crypto. Also check reserved upper bytes from Algorithm 10; first failure order is permissions/reserved/metadata/marker.
Legacy authentication remains user-first if the same bytes match both passwords; these algorithms do not specify an invocation order.

Follow the explicitly described password padding operation and the padding string in Algorithm 2(a); the cross-references pointing at Algorithm 2(b), which is the MD5 initialization step, are inconsistent.

recovery_review.note: Literal EOL preservation, zero hash-padding removal and unsigned-P reinterpretation are reported repairs rather than normative parsing rules. No additional discrepancy was identified in that file; they are not marked verified standard behaviour.

corrected_oracles.crypto/r4-key7: The former successful-authentication expectation allowed an invalid 56-bit V=4 file key. Table 20 requires 128 bits, so this is now a syntax-rejection vector. R3 five- and seven-byte vectors continue to check the variable-length derivation math.

primitive_primary_texts.method: Read algorithm sections and Appendix A.5; numerical constants and counts checked against equations and the Rust implementation. No reference implementation was copied.
Read SHA-256/384/512 functions, constants, preprocessing and computation; compared all printed constants and initial words. The generator recomputes fractional roots using exact integer arithmetic.

Read finite-field definitions, cipher/inverse and expansion; compared every substitution entry and every supported Appendix A word. Numeric Appendix B examples are serialized by columns; prose is not redistributed.

primitive_audit_steps.paraphrase: Append one bit, zeros to 448 mod 512, then the low 64 message-length bits in little-endian order.
primitive_audit_steps.implementation: Md5::finalize saves the original bit count, emits 0x80, pads across a block when needed, and appends little-endian length.
primitive_audit_steps.vectors: crypto/hash-padding-abc; crypto/hash-padding-boundaries (all lengths 0..261).

primitive_audit_steps.paraphrase: Parse words little-endian, initialize four specified words, and emit the accumulated state in little-endian order.
primitive_audit_steps.implementation: All four initial words and parsing/output conversions match.
primitive_audit_steps.vectors: rfc1321_suite checks all seven Appendix A.5 messages, including the multi-block message.

primitive_audit_steps.paraphrase: Apply the four Boolean functions and all 64 scheduled message words, sine constants and left rotations, then accumulate modulo 2^32.
primitive_audit_steps.implementation: Every constant and shift matches; each compact message-index expression was checked against the 64 listed operations, including state permutation and feed-forward.
primitive_audit_steps.vectors: crypto/md5-round-constants recomputes all sine constants independently; seven official digest answers and hashlib boundaries cover composition.

primitive_audit_steps.paraphrase: Use word-size-specific choice, majority, rotate/shift functions and the fractional cube-root round constants.
primitive_audit_steps.implementation: All Boolean expressions, rotation/shift counts, 64 32-bit constants and 80 64-bit constants match.
primitive_audit_steps.vectors: crypto/sha2-round-constants exact integer cube-root expectations; independent hashlib digest cases.

primitive_audit_steps.paraphrase: Pad to 448 or 896 bits per block, append 64- or 128-bit big-endian length and parse big-endian words.
primitive_audit_steps.implementation: The 56/112-byte thresholds, two-block padding paths, original bit counts and word conversions agree for byte-aligned messages within the standard length ranges.
primitive_audit_steps.vectors: crypto/hash-padding-abc reproduces both printed abc padding examples; digest comparison against hashlib; all boundary lengths and streaming splits.

primitive_audit_steps.paraphrase: Initialize SHA-256/512 from the first eight square roots and SHA-384 from prime roots nine through sixteen.
primitive_audit_steps.implementation: All 24 initial words match the printed values; SHA-384 has its own IV rather than a truncated SHA-512 IV.
primitive_audit_steps.vectors: crypto/sha2-round-constants independently derives every IV word with exact integer square roots.

primitive_audit_steps.paraphrase: Expand sixteen words to sixty-four with the small sigma recurrences, run the working-state rounds and add back the state.
primitive_audit_steps.implementation: Schedule offsets 2/7/15/16, sigma counts, T1/T2, variable movement and wrapping additions match.
primitive_audit_steps.vectors: hashlib_known_answers_and_streaming; crypto/hash-padding-boundaries and crypto/hash-padding-abc.

primitive_audit_steps.paraphrase: Use eighty 64-bit scheduled words and the 64-bit round functions with modular feed-forward.
primitive_audit_steps.implementation: Schedule bounds, offsets, rotations, T1/T2, working-state movement and wrapping additions match.
primitive_audit_steps.vectors: hashlib_known_answers_and_streaming; crypto/hash-padding-boundaries and crypto/hash-padding-abc.

primitive_audit_steps.paraphrase: Run the SHA-512 computation with the SHA-384 IV and retain the first six final words.
primitive_audit_steps.implementation: Sha384 uses sha64_compress with its own IV and serializes the leftmost 48 bytes.
primitive_audit_steps.vectors: Independent SHA-384 hashlib cases across both block boundaries, printed abc padding and all IV words.

primitive_audit_steps.locator: ISO 32000-2:2020 clause 7.6.4.3.4 Algorithm 2.B; FIPS 180-4 sections 6.5 and 7
primitive_audit_steps.paraphrase: Retain each selected full digest between iterations and select the leftmost 256 bits after the last iteration.
primitive_audit_steps.implementation: modern_hash retains 32/48/64 bytes as selected and returns the first 32 only after termination; it never substitutes SHA-512/256.
primitive_audit_steps.vectors: crypto/r6-hash-truncation-32, -48 and -64 independently use hashlib and the Python encryptor, exercise all selectors and end with each possible digest width.

primitive_audit_steps.paraphrase: Map bytes into columns, operate in the specified binary field, and use ten or fourteen rounds for supported key sizes.
primitive_audit_steps.implementation: Column-major indexing, reduction polynomial 0x11b, XOR addition, multiplication and supported round counts match.
primitive_audit_steps.vectors: Appendix B trace, key-expansion examples and existing AES-128/256 block tests.

primitive_audit_steps.paraphrase: Map zero to zero before the inverse/affine transformation and use the resulting substitution for each byte.
primitive_audit_steps.implementation: Const-generated GF inverse and affine transformation match all 256 printed entries.
primitive_audit_steps.vectors: crypto/aes-substitution-tables.forward is independently represented by the Python table checked against Table 4.

primitive_audit_steps.vectors: crypto/aes-substitution-tables.inverse; Appendix B inverse-transformation checks.

timing_limitations.aes: Table-based: encryption, decryption and key expansion index forward/inverse S-box tables with secret-dependent values. GF multiplication also contains data-dependent branches; execution time and cache accesses can disclose information. No constant-time guarantee or side-channel resistance is claimed.
timing_limitations.context: The intended use is local document processing. A shared browser/process/hardware environment can still permit timing or cache observations. No algorithm rewrite or performance/security certification is implied by this audit.
